newsitem.title: USA: Gannett to buy Asbury Park Press.
newsitem.headline: Gannett to buy Asbury Park Press.

text.p: Gannett Co Inc said Wednesday it has agreed to purchase New Jersey Press Inc, which publishes the Asbury Park Press and Home News & Tribune newspapers and operates In Jersey, an Internet service.
Terms of the deal were not announced.
The Asbury Park Press, founded in 1879, is the second largest newspaper in New Jersey with a daily circulation of about 160,000 and 230,000 on Sunday, Gannett said.
The Home News & Tribune, of East Brunswick, N.J., has about 81,000 daily circulation and 87,000 on Sunday.
One analyst, who declined to be identified, estimated the deal at roughly $75 million.

J. Kendrick Noble, a media consultant, said the acquisition is "consistent with Gannett's strategy of acquiring dominant papers in medium-sized markets. It also solidifies their postion in New Jersey."
The Asbury Park paper is a fairly strong paper in its market, said Noble.

Gannett already owns the Courier News, published in Somerset, N.J., with a subscription area adjoining the Home News & Tribune's Union County and Somerset County service areas to the west, and papers in Vineland and Camden, in the southern part of the state.
New Jersey's largest newspaper is the Newark-based Star Ledger, which is owned by the Newhouse family.
Gannett noted its chief executive, John J. Curley, worked as a reporter for the Press in 1966 and 1967 and as an editor for the News Tribune, now part of the Home News & Tribune, from 1967 to 1969.
